prediction.likelyOutcome: Liability is conceded; the trial will likely confine the landlord's recovery largely to the deficiency-based unpaid rent (~$78,739) plus late fees and prejudgment interest (~$96,072 total), rather than the $538,000 acceleration figure, because Section 10.02(b)'s acceleration remedy appears to apply only where the landlord does not relet. The $300,000 kitchen claim is likely to fail or be sharply reduced for lack of damages proof, while a substantial attorney's fee award (likely near the $67,000 requested) is probable given the statutory and contractual fee bases and the conceded breach.

issues.label: Attorney's Fees Under Statute and Lease

outcome.description: After the bench trial the trial court rendered judgment for the landlord of $96,072.49 (unpaid rent through trial net of replacement-tenant rent, late fees, and prejudgment interest) — the figure the tenant advocated, roughly one-tenth of the more than $900,000 the landlord sought — plus 18% post-judgment interest, and awarded $0 in attorneys' fees. The court of appeals affirmed the damages award and reversed only the denial of attorneys' fees, remanding for a determination of a reasonable fee under the lease.
outcome.finalNote: Damages affirmed; fee denial reversed and remanded.
